title: The Ruby Ridge Standoff
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck recount the Ruby Ridge standoff in northern Idaho, August 1992. They trace the Weaver family's move from Iowa into Christian Identity and survivalist life, the ATF undercover sting that led to Randy Weaver's firearms charges and failure-to-appear warrant, the year-long government surveillance, and the August 1992 shootout that killed Deputy U.S. Marshal William Degan and 14-year-old Sammy Weaver and wounded Kevin Harris. They describe the loosened FBI rules of engagement, the sniper shot that wounded Randy Weaver and killed Vicky Weaver, the negotiations with Bo Gritz, the surrender, and the 1993 trial that acquitted Harris and Weaver of most charges. They also cover civil settlements, the dismissed charges against sniper Lon Horiuchi, the Senate hearings, the prosecution of agent Michael Cahoon, and the link to Oklahoma City. A listener email correcting an earlier episode on porcupines (convergent vs. co-evolution) closes the show.
topics: Sarah Weaver book From Ruby Ridge to Freedom

entities.name: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF)

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Ruby Ridge episode, note its emotional difficulty, and give a two-sentence overview of the 1992 Idaho standoff.

segments.title: Weaver family background and move to Idaho
segments.summary: Vicky and Randy Weaver's marriage, their religious turn toward apocalyptic beliefs, and their move to a defensible property near Naples, Idaho.

segments.title: Life on the compound and Kevin Harris
segments.summary: The family built a compound from scraps, lived off the land, and homeschooled, which was not legal in Idaho at the time. Kevin Harris, a teen from a troubled home, came to stay with them.

segments.title: Christian Identity beliefs and posse comitatus
segments.summary: Explanation of the Christian Identity beliefs the family shared and the Posse Comitatus movement's view of federal law enforcement. Randy Weaver's 1985 Secret Service visit and his 1988 run for sheriff.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-show break.

segments.title: ATF undercover sting and firearms charges
segments.summary: An undercover ATF agent met Randy Weaver at Aryan Nations-linked meetings and eventually bought two sawed-off shotguns. Weaver refused to become an informant, and Vicky wrote defiant letters. Agents posed as stranded motorists to arrest him in 1991, and he was released on bond.

segments.title: Failure to appear and surveillance plans
segments.summary: A trial date letter contained an error, Weaver did not appear on February 20, 1991, and a bench warrant was issued. Authorities began long surveillance and considered plans to cut off water and to lure out Sarah during her menstrual seclusion, which was rejected as kidnapping.

segments.title: Escalation of the federal operation
segments.summary: Hosts argue the small firearms charge did not justify the scale of the operation, citing unsupported claims that Weaver was a major gun supplier and tied to Montana bank robberies. Surveillance methods included neighbors recording plates, phone taps, and aerial photos.

segments.title: Media helicopter and Elisheba's birth
segments.summary: Geraldo Rivera's helicopter flight over the cabin in April 1992 and the disputed claim of being shot at. Elisheba Weaver was born to Vicky and Randy in late 1991 during the surveillance.

segments.title: August 21 1992 approach and dog shooting
segments.summary: Marshals approached the property on the morning of August 21, 1992. The family's dog Striker went out and was shot. Accounts differ on who fired first.

segments.title: Shootout and deaths of Degan and Sammy Weaver
segments.summary: Sammy Weaver shot at the agents and was killed while retreating. Deputy Marshal William Degan was killed; Kevin Harris is confirmed as the shooter. Randy and Kevin returned to retrieve Sammy's body, and the marshals' sniper claims were disputed.

segments.title: Revised FBI rules of engagement
segments.summary: Hosts describe the FBI's altered rules of engagement, approved by Larry Potts, allowing agents to shoot any armed adult male not endangering a child.

segments.title: Vicky Weaver killed by sniper
segments.summary: FBI sniper Lon Horiuchi shot Randy in the arm, then fired a second shot that killed Vicky Weaver as she held the door holding her infant. Authorities did not immediately realize she was dead and continued addressing her through loudspeakers.

segments.title: Siege tactics and failed negotiation
segments.summary: Roadblocks drew protesters, the perimeter closed as buildings were destroyed, and Sammy's body was found. A remote robot carrying a phone with a mounted gun failed to establish contact. Hosts note Horiuchi's later controversy at Waco.

segments.title: Bo Gritz talks and surrender
segments.summary: Bo Gritz and Jack McClam entered the cabin, brought food for the baby, and helped persuade Randy to come out. Kevin surrendered on August 30 and was taken for medical care. Gritz and a friend took Vicky's body and the pet birds.

segments.title: Final surrender and Jerry Spence
segments.summary: Randy and his three daughters left the cabin under the care of attorney Jerry Spence, who had publicly offered representation. Sarah and Rachel were persuaded to put down their guns.

segments.title: 1993 trial, acquittals, and civil settlements
segments.summary: Randy Weaver and Kevin Harris were charged. The April 1993 trial ended in July with Harris acquitted of all charges and Weaver acquitted except for failure to appear. Family wrongful death suits were settled by the government in 1994, and Harris later received another settlement in 2000.

segments.title: Horiuchi charges and official inquiries
segments.summary: Manslaughter charges against Lon Horiuchi were dismissed. The Senate hearings in 1995, featuring Fred Thompson, and the Justice Department inquiry found the operation badly run. FBI agent Michael Cahoon received an 18-month sentence for destroying an after-action report.

segments.title: Aftermath, Sarah Weaver, and militia movement
segments.summary: Randy Weaver died at age 74. Sarah Weaver wrote a book and forgave the agents. Hosts discuss how Ruby Ridge fueled far-right militias until the Oklahoma City bombing dampened support.

segments.title: Future episode plans
segments.summary: Hosts plan future episodes on Waco and the Oklahoma City bombing.

segments.title: Listener mail: porcupine evolution correction
segments.summary: A listener corrects an earlier porcupine episode, explaining convergent evolution versus co-evolution. Hosts plan to clarify in an upcoming peacock episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and give the show's contact information and credits.
